single connected pathway: train-only successor statistics -> the behaviour tangent t_i at the item's ball point -> its coordinate unit direction n_i and magnitude M_i -> the arc length m_i -> the Mobius translation of the fine code u_k to q_{i,k} -> the framework's metric C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, q_{i,k}) -> the baseline's balanced plan -> the assignment, whose codebook rows are trained through the plan's straight-through estimator. Removing the behaviour sets n_i and m_i identically to zero, q_{i,k} = u_k, and the pathway collapses to the plain metric; removing curvature replaces the lift, the Mobius addition and the distance by their Euclidean limits, and the displacement becomes a flat shift.

Nothing else; no user ids, no timestamps, no popularity signal.

One pass over the training split sequences only (the same split the encoder is trained on). For every adjacent pair (i, s) inside a training sequence increment w_is; store S_i as a sparse row of (s, w_is). W_i = sum_s w_is. No pruning threshold and no top-K: all successors are kept with their counts, so no tuned constant enters. Successor ball points v_s are read from the per-epoch snapshot table indexed by item, so the field refreshes once per epoch and is detached.

behavioral_evidence.value: Train-only expected directed-transition displacement per item (a divergent behaviour field: where the training sequences take you from item i, in embedding space), with its magnitude s_i used as the transport length.

Built once per epoch from the TRAIN split only: for each item i, count directed transitions i -> j where j is the next item of the same training sequence, aggregate over users, row-normalise to w_ij, then b_i = sum_j w_ij (phi_j - phi_i) with phi = stop-gradient of the current encoder item embedding table (24556 rows). Items with zero outgoing train transitions get b_i = 0 and therefore exactly the baseline fine-level cost. Nothing is computed from validation or test, and no gradient flows through phi.

The transition matrix is counted only over training-split sequences; the item embedding table used for phi is fit on training interactions only and is read with stop-gradient, so the behaviour field can neither see a validation/test interaction nor backpropagate into the encoder; the L2/L3 Sinkhorn cost is computed only over training items, and the SID construction never reads validation or test sequences, so no validation or test interaction can enter the Semantic IDs. Validation is used only for after-the-fact diagnostics and Stage3 test is touched once.

behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions from the training split, turned into a per-item latent successor centroid whose tangential component defines the residual direction bias.

From the training split only, count directed adjacent (i to j) co-occurrence inside each training user sequence. Form PMI_ij = log( count_ij * T / (count_i * count_j) ) with T the total training pair count, clip negative values to zero, keep at most 32 successors per item by descending PMI, and row-normalize to weights w_ij. Multiply the stop-gradient encode-side latents of the successors: h_i = sum_j w_ij sg(z_j), then b_i = normalize(h_i - z_i). Everything is recomputed once per epoch from the current encoder latents with the transition counts fixed; no validation or test sequence is ever counted.

SID construction reads only training-split sequences and the encoder latents of training items. The transition counts, the PPMI weights, the successor centroids, the medians R_l and the temperature scale ratios are all measured on the 24556 training items before any validation or test pass, and the SIDs are exported once from that training-only quantizer; Stage 3 then uses them as fixed strings. No validation or test item, sequence, prefix or statistic enters the cost matrix, so the curvature and the behaviour direction carry zero test information and cannot overfit the evaluation split by construction.

ideas.motivation: round_20261106_020541_888 fixed L1 (Hard ER 16.39->6.36, 256/256 codes) but merged the fine layer (955 distinct L2 prefixes vs 7414; weighted 3-level collision 0.771 vs 0.065) and was refused before Stage3. Coarse re-drawing ate the fine resolution: once L1 absorbed the within-cluster variance the residual had nothing left to separate. Fix: never redraw L1; spend behaviour+curvature on making the level-2 code behaviourally predictive, since a TIGER-style decoder commits token 2 before token 3, so an L2 code naming the coarse neighbourhood the item leads to is directly usable.
ideas.novelty: Not a coarse re-weighting, not a Euclidean behaviour suffix, not a side loss. Training transitions are projected INTO the same Poincare ball through the coarse codebook (exp-of-log-mean successor anchor b_i) and enter as the second term of the level-2 cost matrix the baseline Sinkhorn plan already consumes; L1 and L3 stay byte-identical. The term is a DIFFERENTIATOR, not the attractor-to-one-shared-rank that merged items last round; anti-collapse rests on the baseline column marginals, which a cost-only term cannot escape.
ideas.observables: distinct L2 prefixes (>= ~7414, not 955); weighted 3-level collision (<= 0.275); L1 code usage (baseline, L1 untouched); MI(L2 code; successor coarse group) on train data; Stage-3 teacher-forced token-2 accuracy given correct token 1; Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.

specification.text: L1 cost, plan and codebook unchanged (asserted equal at step 0). Per epoch, from the Stage-2 training split only: S_i = top-M directed successors of item i (M = ceil(median positive out-degree), cap 20; |S_i|<2 gives beta_i=0); b_i = exp_0^k((1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} log_0^k(u_{g(j)})), u_{g(j)} the detached L1 code embedding of successor j; stored detached (24556 x d). Per step, inside each L1 group over the 256 L2 codes: d2_r = d_k(r_i,c_k)^2, d2_b = d_k(b_i,c_k)^2, a_i = median_k d2_r, m_i = median_k d2_b (floored at 1e-8), C2 = d2_r/a_i - beta_i*d2_b/m_i, P2 = baseline level-2 Sinkhorn(C2) with the baseline's iterations, marginals and temperature. beta_i = 1 is the documented neutral default because both terms are median-normalised to one per-row scale, so no weight is chosen by trying values. No argmin anywhere; kappa = 1 fixed via model/poincare_contract.

ideas.title: Level-1 untouched; a successor-anchored Poincare term inside the level-2 Sinkhorn cost so the fine SID token encodes where the item leads

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The same code with bhat_i := 0 for all items (hence eta_i = 0, the Mobius translation is the identity): levels 2 and 3 score d_P(r, q_k) with the curved metric only, everything else identical. This arm exists and is correct in the code but is NOT trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The coupled run described here (behaviour transport inside the Poincare distance inside the baseline balanced fine-level assignment) is the one and only arm trained, once, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The same code with the curved operation replaced by the Euclidean one: transport becomes the plain additive shift x_i = u_i + eta_i bhat_i, the cost becomes ||x_i - q^{(l)}_k||^2, and the same baseline Sinkhorn rule is applied. This arm exists and is correct in the code but is NOT trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: Built once per epoch from the TRAIN split only: for each item i, count directed transitions i -> j where j is the next item of the same training sequence, aggregate over users, row-normalise to w_ij, then b_i = sum_j w_ij (phi_j - phi_i) with phi = stop-gradient of the current encoder item embedding table (24556 rows). Items with zero outgoing train transitions get b_i = 0 and therefore exactly the baseline fine-level cost. Nothing is computed from validation or test, and no gradient flows through phi.
ideas.behavior_signal: Train-only expected directed-transition displacement per item (a divergent behaviour field: where the training sequences take you from item i, in embedding space), with its magnitude s_i used as the transport length.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, B ~= 1023 items): two extra Poincare cost matrices of 1023 x 256 x D (about 17 MFLOP each at D = 64), two Mobius translations and two arctanh/clamp passes, ballpark 60 MFLOP and about +2 to +4 ms per step, i.e. about +3 to +5% wall clock over 72000 steps (roughly +3 to +5 minutes on the 3000-epoch four-card run). No extra epochs, no extra forward pass (the behaviour field reuses the existing item embedding table and a precomputed sparse transition matrix storing only observed train pairs), and no new learnable constant.
ideas.coupling_equation: C^{(l)}_{i,k} = d_P( r^{(l-1)}_i (+)_c [ eta_i(s_i, b_i) * bhat_i ] , q^{(l)}_k ), l in {2,3}, with the behaviour term eta_i*bhat_i = rho_l * tanh(s_i/sbar) * b_i/||b_i||, the curved term d_P (Poincare geodesic distance, curvature -1) and (+)_c the Mobius geodesic translation; the plan is the baseline Sinkhorn plan on C^{(l)}/tau.
ideas.coupling_path: One connected pathway: the train-only transition field sets the direction bhat_i and strength s_i; these set the Mobius translation of the item's own residual; the translated residual x_i enters the Poincare distance that forms the L2 (and then L3) Sinkhorn cost matrix; the balanced plan chooses the fine codewords and hence the residual handed to the next level and the resulting SID prefix. Removing the behaviour (bhat = 0) makes the translation the identity and every level-2/3 cost collapses to the pure Poincare residual distance; removing the curvature (Euclidean add + Euclidean cost) removes the ball, the conformal factor and the geodesic structure from the same cost matrix. Either removal changes the same cost matrix, so the coupling is real and not a side loss.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the fine-level collapse came from behaviourally distinct items having residuals too close for the L2/L3 codebooks to separate, then a bounded isometric behaviour translation will restore fine resolution while keeping level 1 intact: distinct L2 prefixes should rise from 955 to at least the baseline order of magnitude (target >= 4000, ideally >= 7414), weighted 3-level collision should fall from 0.771 toward the 0.275 baseline and below the 35% owner gate, level-1 Hard ER should stay near the baseline 16.39 with >= 241/256 level-1 codes used, and prefix behaviour predictability (top-1 next item from the (L1,L2) prefix via train-only adjacency) should rise versus an Euclidean arm. The judgement is Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 in the single 3000-epoch run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantisation of the fine levels: it acts on the residual that levels 2 and 3 quantise, and on the cost matrix of the baseline balanced (Sinkhorn) assignment at those two levels. Level 1 and the encoder loss are untouched.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Mobius addition / exp-map geodesic translation x = u (+)_c eta_i bhat_i inside the Poincare ball of fixed curvature c = 1 (curvature -1, from model/poincare_contract), followed by the Poincare geodesic distance d_P(x,q_k) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||x-q||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||q||^2))); no trainable curvature, so there is no curvature knob to tune.
ideas.key_change: For levels 2 and 3 only, the residual r that the Sinkhorn cost matrix scores is replaced by x = r (+)_c eta_i * bhat_i (a Poincare-ball geodesic translation whose direction is the item's train-only expected transition displacement and whose length is a batch-measured, bounded scale), and the cost becomes the Poincare distance d_P(x, q_k) to the code centroid; the balanced assignment rule, marginals, temperature and solver iterations are the baseline's, unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition matrix is counted only over training-split sequences; the item embedding table used for phi is fit on training interactions only and is read with stop-gradient, so the behaviour field can neither see a validation/test interaction nor backpropagate into the encoder; the L2/L3 Sinkhorn cost is computed only over training items, and the SID construction never reads validation or test sequences, so no validation or test interaction can enter the Semantic IDs. Validation is used only for after-the-fact diagnostics and Stage3 test is touched once.
ideas.motivation: The rejected round biased the LEVEL-1 Sinkhorn cost with a behaviour cohesion reward. It bought the coarse level (Hard ER 16.39 -> 6.36, 256/256 codes, max 0.54%) and destroyed the fine levels: 955 distinct L2 prefixes (baseline 7414, resample reference 16145), weighted 3-level collision 0.771 (reference 0.065), refused at the 35% collision gate, so no Stage3 and no test_R@10. The real recommender problem is that the low-order digits of a Semantic ID must keep enough resolution to separate items that share a coarse category but are consumed very differently, otherwise the generative model cannot condition its next-item distribution finely enough on the prefix. This idea targets exactly that: keep level 1 as the baseline, and make the residual that levels 2 and 3 quantise carry training-only behaviour, without ever pulling two items onto the same codeword.
ideas.novelty: Different level, different sign, different operator from curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1. (a) Level 1 is untouched (baseline Sinkhorn on the Euclidean distance), so the baseline's 241/256 code usage is inherited unchanged. (b) The behaviour field is a DIVERGENCE (expected directed-transition displacement) instead of a cohesion/compactness reward, so it pushes behaviourally diverging residuals apart rather than together. (c) The curved operation is a Mobius (exp-map) geodesic translation of each item's own residual followed by the Poincare distance; a hyperbolic translation is a bijection and an isometry, so it cannot merge two distinct residual vectors onto one codeword, which structurally excludes the previous round's failure mode. (d) No existing repository mechanism transports residuals: the curvature acts on the residual metric, not on a stratum bias.
ideas.observables: (i) number of distinct level-2 prefixes (rejected round 955; baseline 7414) and level-3 prefix count; (ii) item-weighted three-level collision (rejected round 0.771; baseline 0.275; reference 0.065) against the 35% gate; (iii) level-1 Hard ER and level-1 code usage (baseline 16.39, 241/256), which must stay at baseline by construction; (iv) prefix behaviour predictability: top-1 next-item hit rate when the (L1,L2) prefix is looked up in the train-only adjacency on held-out train sequences; (v) Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 as the single judgement.
risks: The translation is an isometry, so it may mostly permute which codeword a residual lands on without adding next-item information, leaving Recall flat while the collision gate passes.; eta_i may saturate (tanh) and become nearly item-independent if behaviour strengths are uniform, degenerating to a global rotation-like shift.; The hyperbolic conformal factor blows distances up near the ball boundary, so large-norm residuals could dominate the cost and starve some codes despite Sinkhorn.; The stop-grad item embedding table makes the behaviour field stale within an epoch.; Parent-conditioned level-3 codebooks may still collide independently of the level-2 improvement.; Single-run seed noise is part of the uncertainty.; Behaviour strengths near sbar could give a push of about half a median residual norm, large enough to reshuffle many level-2 assignments at once.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ||x|| <= 0.999/sqrt(c) and likewise ||u|| and ||q||, and clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1 + 1e-8, so the Poincare distance never returns NaN or Inf at the boundary; eps = 1e-8 in every denominator and in the bhat normalisation; eta_i is bounded by rho_l (one median residual norm) and further by tanh, so the translation can never swamp the residual; items with no train transition get eta_i = 0 and hence exactly the baseline fine-level cost, and that fraction is logged; the behaviour field is detached and rebuilt once per epoch so it cannot feed back into the encoder; the step scale is measured (median residual norm, mean behaviour strength) rather than tuned, and the clip bound, curvature, temperature, Sinkhorn iterations and usage weights all inherit baseline values, so the run needs no sweep; an assert checks that the level-1 cost matrix and plan are bit-identical to the baseline path, which protects the 241/256 usage and the Sinkhorn balancing; a divergence check asserts that the number of distinct level-2 codes used does not fall below the baseline's in the first epochs.
ideas.spec_equations: p = eta_i * bhat_i with eta_i = rho_l * tanh(s_i/(sbar+1e-8)), rho_l = median_batch ||u_i||, sbar = mean_batch s_i, s_i = ||b_i||, b_i = sum_j w_ij (phi_j - phi_i), w_ij = A_ij / sum_j' A_ij', phi_j = sg[E_j]; Mobius sum x = ((1+2c<u,p>+c||p||^2)u + (1-c||u||^2)p)/(1+2c<u,p>+c^2||u||^2||p||^2); d_P(a,b) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||a-b||^2/((1-c||a||^2)(1-c||b||^2))); C^{(l)}_{i,k} = d_P(x_i, q^{(l)}_k); P^{(l)} = Sinkhorn(C^{(l)}/tau, baseline marginals, baseline iterations); k_l(i) from P^{(l)} as baseline; r^{(l)}_i = x_i - q^{(l)}_{k_l(i)}. Per step: gather z for the batch -> baseline level-1 plan (untouched) -> r1 = z - e1 -> for l in 2,3: u = r^(l-1); rho = median||u||.detach(); eta = rho*tanh(s/(sbar+eps)); x = mobius_add(u, eta*bhat, c); C = poincare_dist(x, q^(l), c); plan = baseline_sinkhorn(C/tau); assign k_l; r^(l) = x - q^(l)_{k_l}. The behaviour field is recomputed once per epoch before the epoch's steps, detached.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z_i (D-dim), the baseline level-1 code e1_{k1(i)}, the code centroids q^{(l)}_k for l in {2,3} (parent-conditioned on the chosen grandparent prefix as in the baseline), the train-only sparse transition matrix A and the current encoder item embedding table E, the fixed curvature c from poincare_contract, and the baseline Sinkhorn hyperparameters. Outputs: the level-2 and level-3 code indices for every item (hence the full Semantic ID), the level-2 and level-3 Sinkhorn plans, plus diagnostics (eta distribution, median residual norm, fraction of items with bhat = 0, prefix counts, collision).

specification.text: D is the encoder width as given, c the fixed ball curvature taken from model/poincare_contract (c = 1, curvature -1), K the per-level codebook size as baseline, B ~= 1023 items/step. (1) Train-only behaviour field, refreshed once per epoch with stop-gradient: A_ij = #{train transitions item_t=i -> item_{t+1}=j}; w_ij = A_ij / sum_j' A_ij'; phi_j = sg[E_j] with E the encoder item embedding table; b_i = sum_j w_ij (phi_j - phi_i), s_i = ||b_i||, bhat_i = b_i/(s_i+1e-8), and bhat_i = 0 for items with no outgoing train transition. (2) Level 1: exactly baseline, k1(i) from the baseline Sinkhorn plan on the Euclidean cost; r1_i = z_i - e1_{k1(i)}. (3) For l in {2,3}: u_i = r^{(l-1)}_i; rho_l = median_i ||u_i|| over the batch (detached); sbar = mean_i s_i over the batch (detached); eta_i = rho_l * tanh(s_i/(sbar+1e-8)); x_i = u_i (+)_c eta_i bhat_i with the explicit Mobius sum x = ((1+2c<u,p>+c||p||^2)u + (1-c||u||^2)p)/(1+2c<u,p>+c^2||u||^2||p||^2), p = eta_i bhat_i; cost C^{(l)}_{i,k} = d_P(x_i, q^{(l)}_k) with d_P(a,b) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||a-b||^2/((1-c||a||^2)(1-c||b||^2))); then the baseline Sinkhorn solver on C^{(l)}/tau with the baseline marginals and iteration count produces the plan and the code index is taken from it exactly as baseline; r^{(l)}_i = x_i - q^{(l)}_{k_l(i)}.

ideas.title: Behaviour-transported hyperbolic residual coding: levels 2 and 3 quantise a per-item geodesically shifted residual, never a re-stratified level 1

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same code with the behaviour bias zeroed (u_i = 0 everywhere), so the cost is the pure curvature-scaled Poincare residual distance; the plan and the gradients still change because the tangential term is gone. Exists in the code, never trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: behaviour-rotated residual direction inside the curvature-scaled Poincare cost at levels 2 and 3, baseline Sinkhorn balance and baseline level 1, trained once for 3000 epochs on four cards, judged by Stage3 test Recall@10.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same code with the curved distance replaced by the flat Euclidean cost || r_i + ||r_i|| u_i - c_k ||^2 while keeping the behaviour-rotated residual, so the conformal anisotropy is gone but the behaviour direction survives. Exists in the code, never trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, count directed adjacent (i to j) co-occurrence inside each training user sequence. Form PMI_ij = log( count_ij * T / (count_i * count_j) ) with T the total training pair count, clip negative values to zero, keep at most 32 successors per item by descending PMI, and row-normalize to weights w_ij. Multiply the stop-gradient encode-side latents of the successors: h_i = sum_j w_ij sg(z_j), then b_i = normalize(h_i - z_i). Everything is recomputed once per epoch from the current encoder latents with the transition counts fixed; no validation or test sequence is ever counted.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions from the training split, turned into a per-item latent successor centroid whose tangential component defines the residual direction bias.
ideas.cost_estimate: Under 5 percent wall clock for the single frozen 3000-epoch, four-card run, and no extra parameters. Per-step at the frozen scale (batch 1024, 24 steps per epoch, 24556 training items): two extra 1024x256 cost matrices with an arcosh each, about 0.04 GFLOP per step at d=64, well under 1 percent of a transformer step, plus two Sinkhorn plans of the size the baseline already solves at every level. Per-epoch: one sparse successor-centroid table, at most 24556x32 non-zeros times d, about 0.05 GFLOP against roughly 240 GFLOP of training steps per epoch; two medians over 24556 values. Memory: one 24556 x d behaviour table (about 6 MB at d=64) and two 256 x d ball-embedded codebooks.
ideas.coupling_equation: C^l_{ik} = (1/sqrt(|kappa_l|)) * arcosh( 1 + 2|kappa_l| ||p_i - e_k||^2 / ((1-|kappa_l|||p_i||^2)(1-|kappa_l|||e_k||^2)) ) with p_i = tanh(||r_i^l|| / (2 R_l)) * normalize( rhat_i^l + normalize(h_i - z_i)_tangential ), i.e. the curved term is d_poincare_kappa( . , . ) and the behaviour term is the tangential successor-centroid rotation normalize(rhat + u), both inside the same cost entry that feeds the baseline Sinkhorn plan.
ideas.coupling_path: One connected path: training transitions -> PPMI successor centroid h_i -> tangential behaviour direction u_i -> behaviour-rotated unit residual v_i -> lifted ball point p_i = tanh(||r_i||/2R_l) * v_i -> Poincare cost C^l(i,k) against the ball-lifted codewords -> baseline Sinkhorn plan -> level-l code index and the reconstruction gradient on codebooks and encoder. Remove the behaviour (u_i = 0) and p_i becomes the plain radial lift, so every cost entry, plan entry and gradient changes; remove the curvature (Euclidean cost on r_i + ||r_i|| u_i) and the conformal anisotropy disappears, so the same plan and gradients change again.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the coupling is real then, at fixed Sinkhorn balance and with L1 bit-identical to the baseline, the level-2 and level-3 residual directions of behaviourally distinct items become separable under the conformal metric, so codes are reused across coarse regimes instead of inside one: distinct L2 prefixes must stay at or above the frozen baseline's 7414 (and weighted 3-level collision at or below 0.275) instead of collapsing toward the rejected round's 955 and 0.771, level-2 codebook usage must stay broad, and the one allowed Stage3 run must give test Recall@10 above 0.065. If L2 prefix counts stay flat while Stage3 recall also stays flat, the behaviour direction carried no fine-layer information and the idea is dead on one run, no ablation needed.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer at levels 2 and 3, in the cost matrix of the balanced Sinkhorn assignment, both at every training step (the code indices used for reconstruction and the gradients they carry) and at the final SID export; level 1 is left on the baseline Euclidean cost.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance with fixed negative curvature kappa_l = -1/R_l^2, R_l the measured training median residual norm of level l: d(x,y) = (1/sqrt(|kappa_l|)) * arcosh(1 + 2|kappa_l| ||x-y||^2 / ((1 - |kappa_l| ||x||^2)(1 - |kappa_l| ||y||^2))), together with the radial exp_0 map a = tanh(||r|| / (2 R_l)) that places each residual at a curvature-consistent radius.
ideas.key_change: At levels 2 and 3, replace the Euclidean residual-to-codeword cost inside the baseline Sinkhorn plan by a Poincare-ball distance between (a) the item residual lifted by tanh(||r||/2R_l) along a behaviour-rotated unit direction and (b) the codebook vector lifted by the same radial map; the assignment rule, its uniform marginals and its balancing are unchanged, only the cost matrix changes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: SID construction reads only training-split sequences and the encoder latents of training items. The transition counts, the PPMI weights, the successor centroids, the medians R_l and the temperature scale ratios are all measured on the 24556 training items before any validation or test pass, and the SIDs are exported once from that training-only quantizer; Stage 3 then uses them as fixed strings. No validation or test item, sequence, prefix or statistic enters the cost matrix, so the curvature and the behaviour direction carry zero test information and cannot overfit the evaluation split by construction.
ideas.motivation: The rejected round proved coarse layers can be re-drawn by behaviour (L1 Hard ER 16.39->6.36, all 256 L1 codes used) but that doing so eats fine-layer resolution: only 955 distinct L2 prefixes against 7414 in the frozen baseline, weighted 3-level collision 0.771 against 0.275, refused before Stage3 because the coarse partition had already consumed the behaviour cohesion and left residuals small, magnitude-dominated and mutually aligned. The recommendation problem this attacks is exactly that: the first Semantic-ID token decides the coarse regime, but the second and third tokens, which are what makes a 3-level SID address 24556 items instead of 256, lose their discriminative power. The fix must add fine-layer separability without re-partitioning the coarse layer.
ideas.novelty: Different from curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1 in four coupled ways: (1) the behaviour quantity is a vector, not a scalar rank - a popularity-adjusted successor centroid in latent space rotated onto the residual tangent - so it changes the *direction* of a residual, not the level it belongs to; (2) it acts only at levels 2 and 3, with the L1 cost matrix provably bit-identical to the frozen baseline, so the coarse occupancy budget is untouched; (3) the curvature is not a stratification rho_i against a stratum centre, it is a conformal metric on residual directions with kappa_l = -1/R_l^2 where R_l is the measured training median residual norm of that level, i.e. the geometry is derived from the level's own residual scale; (4) the behaviour bias is applied as an angle in the ball, so it cannot influence the radial coordinate and therefore cannot pull items onto a shared fine code. No existing mechanism here couples a directed-transition latent centroid with a conformal Poincare residual metric inside the balanced Sinkhorn cost.
ideas.observables: Distinct L2 prefix count and weighted 3-level collision rate recorded every epoch (diagnostic, not a gate); level-2 and level-3 codebook usage histograms; the fraction of items whose level-2 index differs from the behaviour-off cost; level-2 reconstruction loss; the Sinkhorn marginals and the L1 plan checked bit-identical to the baseline; finally Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 on the single run.
risks: The behaviour direction for low-degree or cold training items is noisy or zero; if a large fraction of items has no positive-PPMI successor, the effectively coupled subset is small and the fine-layer gain never reaches Stage3.; Conformal amplification near the ball boundary can over-penalize large-residual items and push their L2 indices into a narrow angular sector, which would trade the old collapse for a new one.; The Sinkhorn balance fights an anisotropic cost: marginals stay uniform but the plan may saturate, and the entropy temperature rescaling could make the plan nearly hard and destabilize codebook updates.; tanh radial compression loses resolution among the very small residuals that dominate inside a well-separated L1 code, so level-3 could lose rather than gain prefix variety.; Behaviour built from training transitions reinforces popularity head behaviour and can homogenize the fine codes of long-tail items that actually carry much of Recall@10.; A single run with seed noise: if the effect is smaller than run-to-run recall variance, the mechanism cannot be distinguished from noise at this budget.
ideas.safeguards: Radial argument clipped to [0,3] before tanh so a_i <= 1 - 1e-9 and the conformal denominator is floored at 1e-6; arcosh argument clamped at 1+1e-7; normalization epsilon 1e-8; u_i set to zero when the item has no positive-PPMI successor or when ||r_i|| < 1e-6; R_l floored at 1e-6 and recomputed as a detached training median once per epoch; eps_l rescaled scale-relatively and never swept; stop-grad on successor latents, on R_l and on the temperature ratio so behaviour cannot be gamed by shrinking latents; the level-1 cost matrix, marginals and plan are asserted bit-identical to the baseline by a unit check, and Sinkhorn marginals are asserted uniform after every plan, so the balancing that keeps codebook usage even is provably the baseline's; per-epoch distinct-prefix and collision counters are logged as diagnostics only, never used as an admission gate.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) w = row_normalize( top32( max(0, log( count_ij * T / (count_i * count_j) ) ) ) ) over training adjacent pairs. 2) h_i = sum_j w_ij sg(z_j); b_i = normalize(h_i - z_i); rhat_i = r_i / (||r_i|| + 1e-8); u_i = b_i - (b_i . rhat_i) rhat_i, zeroed if no successor. 3) v_i = normalize(rhat_i + u_i); a_i = tanh( clip(||r_i|| / (2 R_l), 0, 3) ); p_i = a_i v_i. 4) e_k = tanh( clip(||c_k|| / (2 R_l), 0, 3) ) * normalize(c_k). 5) d_ik = (1/sqrt(|kappa_l|)) * arcosh( clamp(1 + 2|kappa_l| ||p_i - e_k||^2 / ( max(1 - |kappa_l|||p_i||^2, 1e-6) * max(1 - |kappa_l|||e_k||^2, 1e-6) ), min=1+1e-7) ). 6) C^l = d; eps_l = eps_base * mean(C^l) / mean(C^l_euclid) (detached, once per epoch). 7) Pi = sinkhorn(C^l, uniform marginals, eps_l, baseline iterations); index_l(i) = argmax_k Pi_ik. 8) level 1: C^1 and Pi^1 identical to the frozen baseline.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latents z_i of the training batch, the item residuals r_i^l at levels 2 and 3, the current codewords c_k^l, the fixed sparse PPMI successor matrix W (24556 x 24556, at most 32 non-zeros per row), the per-epoch stop-gradient latent matrix Z (24556 x d), and the baseline Sinkhorn configuration (marginals, iterations, eps_base). Outputs: a behaviour vector h_i and tangential direction u_i per item, curvature-scaled cost matrices C^2, C^3 of shape batch x 256, balanced transport plans Pi^2, Pi^3, integer level-2 and level-3 indices, and the differentiable graph that carries the reconstruction gradient back into the codewords and the encoder; at export, the same routine returns the frozen 3-level SID strings.

specification.text: Notation: z_i encoder output (decode-side latent) for training item i, c^1_{k1(i)} its frozen-baseline level-1 codeword, r_i^l the level-l residual (r^2 = z - c^1, r^3 = z - c^1 - c^2). Level 1 is untouched: C^1 is the baseline cost and the baseline plan is reused verbatim. Training-only behaviour: PPMI-clipped directed transition successors. For each level l in {2,3} and each epoch: (1) measure R_l = median_i ||r_i^l|| over the 24556 training items (detached, no gradient) and set kappa_l = -1/R_l^2; (2) build the successor centroid h_i = sum_j w_ij sg(z_j), w_ij the row-normalized positive-PPMI weights, capped at 32 successors, sg = stop-grad; (3) unit residual rhat_i = r_i/||r_i||, behaviour tangent b_i = normalize(h_i - z_i), tangential part u_i = b_i - (b_i . rhat_i) rhat_i (zero if the item has no positive-PPMI successor or ||r_i|| < 1e-6); (4) behaviour-rotated direction v_i = normalize(rhat_i + u_i); (5) radial coordinate a_i = tanh(||r_i|| / (2 R_l)); (6) lifted points p_i = a_i v_i and e_k = tanh(||c_k|| / (2 R_l)) * normalize(c_k); (7) cost C^l_{ik} = (1/sqrt(|kappa_l|)) * arcosh(1 + 2|kappa_l| ||p_i - e_k||^2 / ((1 - |kappa_l| ||p_i||^2)(1 - |kappa_l| ||e_k||^2))); (8) Sinkhorn with the baseline rule and the baseline marginals on C^l, temperature rescaled scale-relatively as eps_l = eps_base * mean(C^l) / mean(C^l_euclid) computed detached once per epoch, and take the plan's argmax column as the level-l index; (9) codebook and encoder gradients flow through the plan and through C^l, hence through the behaviour direction, so the behaviour changes parameter updates, not only indices. Collapse guards are structural, not tuned: behaviour never enters the radius a_i, never enters level 1, and never enters the marginals.

ideas.title: Poincare Conformal Residual-Direction Sinkhorn: train-only transition-direction bias on levels 2-3 under a curvature set by the measured residual scale

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAV=off sets t_i = 0 for every item, so n_i = 0 and m_i = 0, q_{i,k} = u_k, and the fine-level Sinkhorn cost is the pure Poincare distance d_P(v_i, u_k). Everything else, including the balanced plan and the curvature, is unchanged. The switch exists and is unit-checked; this arm is not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAV=on and GEOM=poincare, i.e. exactly the mechanism above: successor-derived geodesic code displacement with exact Poincare distance inside the baseline balanced plan. This is the only arm that is trained, once, for 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards followed by the frozen Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOM=euclid sets c := 0 for the COST only: the lift becomes the LINEAR map v = r/q_l, Mobius addition becomes vector addition and the distance becomes d_0(x,y) = 2||x-y||. The behaviour field (t_i, n_i, M_i, m_i) is computed with the CURVED operators (c = 1) in BOTH arms, so the Euclidean arm displaces the codes exactly as the curved arm does and the two arms differ in the METRIC only. The arm is unit-checked and not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split sequences only (the same split the encoder is trained on). For every adjacent pair (i, s) inside a training sequence increment w_is; store S_i as a sparse row of (s, w_is). W_i = sum_s w_is. No pruning threshold and no top-K: all successors are kept with their counts, so no tuned constant enters. Successor ball points v_s are read from the per-epoch snapshot table indexed by item, so the field refreshes once per epoch and is detached.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions in the training split: for each item i, the multiset of items s that occur immediately after i in a training user sequence, with their counts w_is (sequential co-consumption of a directed, successor form). Nothing else; no user ids, no timestamps, no popularity signal.
ideas.cost_estimate: Frozen scale 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch (about 1023 items per step), 3000 epochs. Per step: extra 2 levels * 1023 items * 256 codes = 524k Mobius-add + artanh + norm evaluations at d = 32, about 0.07 GFLOP, under 1% of the encoder forward+backward. Per epoch: one extra forward-only pass over all 24556 items (24 forward batches, no backward) to refresh the successor snapshot, about one third of an epoch's forward cost, so roughly +5% to +7% wall clock per epoch and about the same over the whole run. No extra epochs, no extra seeds, no extra arms.
ideas.coupling_equation: C[i,k] = d_P^c( v_i , u_k (+) ( tanh(sqrt(c) m_i / 2)/sqrt(c) ) * n_i ), with m_i n_i = clip_{0.5 * min_j d_P(v_i,u_j)}( M_i ), M_i = ||t_i||_2 the idea's COORDINATE magnitude and n_i = t_i/max(||t_i||_2, 1e-12) the COORDINATE unit direction - the idea's pair, so that d_P(0, Delta_i) = 2||(m_i/2) n_i|| = m_i holds exactly under the framework's factor 2. Both terms of the clip are detached, and the whole behaviour field is detached.
ideas.coupling_path: single connected pathway: train-only successor statistics -> the behaviour tangent t_i at the item's ball point -> its coordinate unit direction n_i and magnitude M_i -> the arc length m_i -> the Mobius translation of the fine code u_k to q_{i,k} -> the framework's metric C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, q_{i,k}) -> the baseline's balanced plan -> the assignment, whose codebook rows are trained through the plan's straight-through estimator. Removing the behaviour sets n_i and m_i identically to zero, q_{i,k} = u_k, and the pathway collapses to the plain metric; removing curvature replaces the lift, the Mobius addition and the distance by their Euclidean limits, and the displacement becomes a flat shift.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the fine-level prefix collapse of the previous round was caused by fine codes being free to crowd behaviourally similar items together, then a repulsive, curvature-amplified code displacement derived from train-only directed transitions must raise the number of distinct L2 prefixes well above 955, push the item-weighted 3-level collision under the 35% gate, leave level-1 ER near the baseline (about 16.4), and give Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. It is worth keeping if the collision rate drops without level-1 ER degrading and recall clears the target; it is refuted if collisions stay above 0.5 or if level-1 ER degrades while recall does not move.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the quantisation step of the RQ-VAE, inside the Sinkhorn cost matrix of levels 2 and 3, before the balanced plan is solved; it changes both which code each fine level assigns (through the plan) and the gradient that reaches the residual encoder and the fine codebooks (through d_P and through the displacement).
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1.0 (K = -1), with the framework's metric d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||), whose c -> 0 limit is 2||x-y||; the idea's informal (1/sqrt(c)) form is CORRECTED to the framework's factor 2, because with the baseline's epsilon fixed the factor doubles the cost and therefore halves the effective entropic temperature of the plan, and the mechanism takes a PLAN rather than an argmin. The ball lift is the frozen-scale origin exponential exp_0^c(r/q_l) = tanh(sqrt(c)||r/q_l||) (r/q_l)/(sqrt(c)||r/q_l||) with the explicit zero limit, and the tangent logarithm is the contract's log_x^c(y) with the 1 - 1e-5 artanh clip and the explicit zero limit.
ideas.key_change: For each item i and each fine-level code k, the code's ball point u_k is translated by Mobius addition along the item's unit behavioural direction n_i by an arc length m_i, and the Sinkhorn cost entry becomes the framework's metric from v_i to that displaced code; the balanced plan itself is the baseline's, applied to the cost matrix itself, and the plan's straight-through estimator x_q = P + (one_hot(k) - P).detach() feeds the decoder the chosen RAW codeword - the forward value is exactly the baseline's - while the reconstruction's gradient reaches the fine levels' CODEBOOK through the plan. The fine levels' item points are constants (the residual chain is a value chain), so the encoder's reconstruction gradient is the baseline's own, and the behaviour field itself is detached and nothing trains it.
ideas.leakage_boundary:
S_i is built exclusively from adjacency pairs inside training-split sequences, computed once before training and frozen for the whole run; validation and test sequences are never read, never encoded into the snapshot, and never used to set q_l, m_i or the clip. The peer-c

lip uses min_k d_P(v_i, u_k) from the current training step only, so nothing about held-out interaction can influence the SID construction, the codebook, or the assigned identifiers. q_l is a percentile of training residuals at epoch 0, also training-only.
ideas.motivation: The previous round proved that behaviour+curvature coupling CAN re-partition the coarse level (L1 Hard ER 16.39 -> 6.36, all 256 level-1 codes used) but that re-partitioning the coarse level spends the fine levels' spatial freedom: only 955 distinct L2 prefixes survived against 7414 in the frozen baseline and 16145 in the reference arm, and the item-weighted 3-level collision rose to 0.771 (reference 0.065), so that arm was refused at the Stage3 gate and Stage3 test Recall@10 was never measured. The real recommender problem here is not coarse semantics, it is that many distinct items are forced to share the same fine prefix, so the generative model cannot emit the right item even when it emits the right coarse token. This idea attacks exactly that: keep the coarse partition as the baseline builds it, and use behaviour+curvature to protect the resolution of the fine levels.
ideas.novelty: Not a cohesion bias on level 1, not a scalar behaviour offset added to a distance, not a second hyperbolic loss. The behaviour signal moves the CODE POINT itself along a hyperbolic geodesic (a Mobius translation of the code inside the Poincare ball) before the distance is taken, so the behaviour term is a geometric displacement of the codebook, not an additive score. It is repulsive by construction (a code already crowded by the item's successors is pushed geodesically away from that item), it acts only on levels 2 and 3, and the curvature is what makes the displacement non-uniform: the same behavioural arc length buys a much larger separation near the ball boundary, where fine residual codes live, than near the origin. No existing mechanism in this repository displaces a code point; existing code either biases a cost additively or runs an independent hyperbolic loss.
ideas.observables: distinct L2 prefix count (from 955 upward, baseline reference 7414), item-weighted 3-level collision rate (from 0.771 toward and below the 0.35 gate), level-1 Hard ER (should stay near the baseline 16.4 instead of moving), per-item entropy of level-2 and level-3 code usage, fraction of fine codes never used, prefix behaviour predictability during Stage 3, and the deciding number: Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
risks: Successor directions may be dominated by a few hub items, injecting noise into n_i; the per-epoch detached snapshot lags the encoder and could misdirect the displacement early in training; the repulsion may fight the Sinkhorn balance enough to degrade the level-2 Euclidean reconstruction or level-1 ER; the tanh lift could saturate near the boundary and freeze the fine codebook; the curvature amplification near the boundary could make the cost matrix ill-conditioned for Sinkhorn (needs the artanh clamp and the half-nearest-code cap); the effect may be too weak relative to the encoder gradient to show in one run, in which case the collision metric is the observable that decides.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped to 1 - 1e-5 in the distance and in the logarithm; the tanh lift bounds every ball point to radius < 1/sqrt(c) so lambda never diverges; m_i is capped at half the distance to the nearest code (scale-relative, no tuned constant, measured per step on training items) and BOTH terms of that cap are detached; the behaviour vector and the whole field are detached, so no cross-item second-order graph and no gradient explosion through successors; the explicit zero limits are used instead of a 1e-12 guard wherever a norm can vanish; cold items with no successors get t_i = 0, hence m_i = 0 (they fall back to the pure Poincare cost); level 1 is excluded so the coarse partition and level-1 ER are not disturbed, and the baseline's level-1 loss terms are kept; the percentile scale q_l is frozen at epoch 0 so the ball geometry cannot drift with training; the Sinkhorn epsilon, the marginals and the plan extraction are the baseline's.
ideas.spec_equations: input residual batch r, codebook E (256 rows), level l in {2,3}, successor sparse rows S_i, snapshot table V_l (item -> ball point), curvature c = 1, scale q_l. l1: v_i = exp_0^c(r_i/q_l); u_k = exp_0^c(E_k/q_l). l2: for each i, t_i = sum_s (w_is/W_i) * log_{v_i}^c(V_l[s]) with the contract's logarithm (the 1 - 1e-5 artanh clip, the explicit zero limit); an item with W_i = 0 has t_i = 0 by definition. if BEHAV=off then m_i = 0, n_i = 0 else n_i = t_i/max(||t_i||_2, 1e-12), M_i = ||t_i||_2, d_nn_i = min_k d_P(v_i, u_k), m_i = min(M_i, 0.5*d_nn_i), with BOTH terms of the clip detached. l3: for each (i,k): q_{i,k} = mobius_add(u_k, (tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)/sqrt(c)) * n_i); C[i,k] = d_P(v_i, q_{i,k}) with the framework's factor 2 (the c -> 0 limit is 2||x-y||). l4: P = baseline_sinkhorn(C, epsilon, uniform_item_marginal, balanced_code_marginal) applied to C itself; the assignment = baseline_plan_to_index(P); x_q = P + (one_hot(k) - P).detach(), whose forward value is the chosen RAW codeword and whose backward carries the reconstruction's gradient into C, v_i and u_k; the residual chain is a value chain, residual = (residual - quant).detach(), which is what the baseline's own quantizer already does. l5: loss = the baseline's RQ-VAE loss over ALL THREE levels (the level-1 commitment and codebook terms included). The snapshot V_l is taken at the START of each epoch, before that epoch's first update, from the epoch-start encoder and the epoch-start assignments. Helper: artanh_arg = min(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||, 1 - 1e-5).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: takes the current batch of fine-level residuals r_i (B x d), the level-l codebook rows E_k (256 x d), the frozen training successor rows S_i with counts, the per-epoch detached successor ball-point snapshot V, the curvature c and the frozen scale q_l; returns the B x 256 cost matrix C (Poincare distance to the behaviour-displaced codes), the balanced Sinkhorn plan P from the baseline rule, and the resulting level-l code indices for the batch, plus the quantities C is built from so the three switches can be toggled.

specification.text:
Per level l in {2,3} (level 1 is deliberately untouched). Let c = 1.0 (fixed negative curvature, K = -1), lambda(x) = 2/(1 - c*||x||^2), Mobius addition x (+) y, and geodesic distance d_P(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) * artanh(sqrt(c) * ||(-x) (+) y||). Residual r_i = z_i - sum_{j<l} e_{k_j(i)} (unchanged baseline residual). Bounded ball lift with a frozen per-level scale q_l measured on the training split at epoch 0 (95th percentile of ||r||): v_i = (1/sqrt(c)) * tanh(sqrt(c)*||r_i||/q_l) * r_i/||r_i||, and u_k = same lift of codebook row e_k. Behaviour: for item i let S_i be its directed successor multiset in the training sequences with counts w_is, and let v_s be the ball points of those successors at level l taken from the per-epoch no-grad snapshot. Tangent behaviour vector at the item t_i = sum_s (w_is/W_i) * Log_{v_i}(v_s); unit direction n_i = t_i/||t_i||; raw magnitude M_i = ||t_

i||. Displaced code q_{i,k} = u_k (+) ( tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)/(sqrt(c)) * n_i ), where m_i = min(M_i, 0.5 * min_k d_P(v_i, u_k)). Cost C[i,k] = d_P(v_i, q_{i,k}). Feed C to the baseline's Sinkhorn (same epsilon, same uniform item marginal, same balanced code marginal, same plan extraction) and take the baseline's assignment; no argmin replaces the plan. t_i and n_i are detached per-epoch constants; gradients flow only through v_i and u_k.

ideas.title: Behaviour-directed geodesic code drift on the fine residual levels: displacing each code along the item's directed-transition direction inside the Poincare ball, inside the baseline Sinkhorn cost, for levels 2 and 3 only.

math_review_findings: conventions.distance and computations.distance: the metric is written d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(min(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||,1-1e-5)) and the whole cost, the nearest-code cap and the displacement identity are built on that factor, while the idea's metric is d_P(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(...). The factor 2 doubles every cost and, with the baseline epsilon held fixed, halves the entropic temperature of the plan, so the plan is not the idea's plan. The specification must carry the idea's factor 1 (and then Delta_i must be exp_0(m_i n_i), without the /2, to keep d_c(0,Delta_i) = m_i); a factor change cannot be introduced by the spec, only by a corrected idea text.

computations.sinkhorn_plan: the note says both 'the mechanism replaces the cost matrix only' (which would keep the baseline's [-1,1] rescaling of distances, hence its temperature) and that, because no rescaling is applied, 'the mechanism's plan runs at a different temperature from the baseline's'. The two statements cannot both be true, and the idea says the cost is fed to the baseline Sinkhorn with the same epsilon. Either C must go through the baseline's own rescaling (then same epsilon means same temperature) or the spec must state that the Sinkhorn epsilon is itself rescaled and the assignment is a different plan; as written the switch between the two claims is ambiguous and the mechanism is not the idea's.

gradient_rules[1] and mechanism: the residual chain is made a value chain (residual = (residual - quant).detach()), so the fine levels' item points v_i are constants and the reconstruction gradient reaches only u_k, while the idea states 't_i and n_i are detached per-epoch constants; gradients flow only through v_i and u_k'. The idea's residual r_{i,l} = z_i - sum_{j<l} e_{k_j} is differentiable in the encoder output z_i, so v_i must stay on the differentiable path to the encoder (no detach on r_{i,2}, r_{i,3}); a removal of the v_i path is a change of the idea, not a faithful formulation.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: t_i is accumulated with log_at(u[edge_item], V[edge_successor], c) on the differentiable u = lift(r, c), and n_i = t_i / clamp(||t_i||), demand_i = (tanh(sqrt(c) m_i/2)/sqrt(c)) n_i, q_ik and C_ik are all built from it with no detach, so the behaviour field carries gradient into the encoder and the codebook. That contradicts both the idea (t_i and n_i are detached per-epoch constants) and gradient_rules[2] (no gradient through the field). t_i, n_i, M_i, d_nn_i, m_i and demand_i must all be computed under .detach()/torch.no_grad().

continuous_surface.executable_statements: after 'a = a / q_l' the quantiser is 'e_l = p_i @ a', i.e. the q_l-scaled codeword E_k/q_l, and 'r_next = r - e_l' subtracts it from the already q_l-scaled residual 'r = r / q_l'. This contradicts computations.quantised_value (q_i = s_i @ E, whose forward value is exactly the RAW codeword E_{k_l(i)}) and training_integration (the chosen RAW, UNLIFTED codeword at every level), and it leaves the level-3 residual divided by q_2 as well as by q_3. The selector must multiply the raw codebook E, and the residual chain must stay in the unscaled units r = z - sum of raw codewords.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: `a = a / q_l` overwrites the codebook with the scaled copy and `e_l = p_i @ a` then builds the quantised vector from E_k/q_l, so the decoder would be fed the SCALED codebook, not the raw codeword. quantised_value, reconstruction and training_integration require the forward value to be exactly the raw, unlifted E_{k_l(i)}; the scaled copy must be a separate variable used only for the lift (`b = lift(E/q_l, c)`), and `e_l` must use the raw E.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: the residual recursion is `r_next = r - e_l` while `r` has already been divided by q_l and `e_l` is also in q_l units, and the `.detach()` of the declared value chain is missing. Re-entering the block with `r = r / q_l` divides the level-3 residual by q_2*q_3 instead of q_3. It must be `r_next = (r_l - E_{k_l}).detach()` in RAW units, normalised once by q_3, exactly as the gradient_rules and level_residual state.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: `d_nn_i = dist(u, b, c)` and `demand_i = (tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)/sqrt(c)) * n_i` are built with the SAME c symbol as the cost, so GEOM=euclid (c := 0) also changes the behaviour field: d_nn_i becomes 2||v_i-u_k||, m_i = min(M_i,0.5*d_nn) and Delta_i change, and the arm no longer 'displaces the codes exactly as the curved arm does'. The field must use a separate frozen constant c_field = 1 (lift, log, d_nn, Delta) in both arms, and only the lift/addition/distance of the COST must take the switch's c.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: `def lift` divides by `sqrt(c)*_norm(v) + eps`, a pole guard that returns ~||v||^2/eps for small ||v|| instead of the vector itself. This contradicts ball_lift's explicit tanhc limit (tanhc(0) = 1, 'no 1e-12 guard stands in for the limit'); the zero limit must be an explicit branch or analytic limit, not an additive epsilon in the denominator.

gradient_rules / residual chain: the specification makes the fine levels' item points v_i constants ('It does NOT reach the fine levels' item points v_i', residual = (residual - quant).detach()), whereas the idea states 'gradients flow only through v_i and u_k'. The cost's gradient therefore never reaches the encoder at levels 2 and 3, changing which parameters the fine-level cost trains; either the fine-level residual must be kept differentiable (no detach) so v_i is in the path, or this must be declared as an explicit recorded amendment, like the factor-2 correction, instead of being justified as 'what the baseline's quantizer already does'.

findings: Distance normalization: `poincare_cost`, `continuous_surface`, and `conventions.distance` use d_c = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(...), while the idea's d_P is (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(...). This doubles the cost and, with the baseline epsilon fixed, changes the Sinkhorn plan; the half-displacement `exp_0((m/2)n)` also relies on the factor 2 to make d_c(0,Delta)=m. The specification must use the idea's factor 1 and adjust the half factor, or explicitly record a corrected factor and amend the idea; it cannot silently change the metric normalization.

Magnitude/direction mismatch: `behaviour_direction` defines n_i = t_i/||t_i|| (Euclidean unit), while `behaviour_magnitude` defines M_i = lambda_{v_i}||t_i|| (Riemannian norm). Then M_i n_i = lambda_{v_i} t_i, whose Riemannian norm at v_i is lambda_{v_i}^2||t_i||, not M_i; the idea's pair is n_i=t_i/||t_i||, M_i=||t_i||. The spec must use either the coordinate pair (M=||t||) or the Riemannian pair (n=t/(lambda||t||), M=lambda||t||), and the displacement must use that same vector.

Gradient path removed: `loss_total` states that NO term in C or q enters the loss and that C/P are decision variables; the idea states gradients flow only through v_i and u_k. With the baseline additive STE the cost's gradient is annihilated, so the displaced cost has no training signal to v_i or u_k; the mechanism only changes hard assignments. The spec must add a differentiable cost/plan term (or straight-through carrier) to the loss, or explicitly amend the idea; as written the idea's gradient path is absent.

Log map clip/zero limit missing: `behaviour_tangent` uses log_x^c(y) = ... atanhc(sqrt(c)||w||) ... with no artanh clip to 1-1e-5 and no atanhc(0)=1 definition, although the idea's helper caps artanh_arg and `poincare_cost` uses the cap. At w=0 this is 0/0; near the boundary it is artanh(1)=inf. It must apply the same 1-1e-5 clip and define atanhc(0)=1.

GEOM=euclid does not keep the behaviour field unchanged: `switch_geometry` claims n_i and m_i keep their values, but `behaviour_tangent`, `behaviour_magnitude`, `nearest_code_distance` and `arc_length` all depend on c; setting c:=0 changes the lift to linear, lambda to 2, d_nn to Euclidean 2||v-u||, hence t_i, M_i, d_nn_i and m_i. The switch must freeze the behaviour field computed under c=1 (or state that it is recomputed and withdraw the 'unchanged' claim); as written it does not do what it says.

Level-1 baseline loss omitted: `loss_total` runs the commitment and codebook terms 'over l in {2,3}', while the idea says level 1 is untouched and the baseline is executed verbatim. Since the STE gives the level-1 codebook no gradient, omitting its codebook/commitment terms leaves level 1 untrained. The loss must include the baseline level-1 terms (e.g. over l in {1,2,3}), with only the cost/drift restricted to l in {2,3}.

Continuous surface undefined at c=0: `continuous_surface.executable_statements` computes displaced_distance as 2*atanh(arg)/sqrt(c) and `_mobius` uses c; at c=0 this divides by zero, and the `statements` C likewise. The GEOM=euclid branch claims the c->0 limit, but the surface cannot be evaluated there. It must branch to d_0=2||x-y|| (and vector addition) or use a stable c->0 formula.

computations.behaviour_tangent: the logarithm is written log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c)*lambda_x^c)) * atanhc(sqrt(c)||w||) * w, w = (-x)(+)y, with no normalisation by ||w||; with atanhc(a)=artanh(a)/a this is (2/(c*lambda_x^c)) artanh(...) w/||w||, a factor 1/sqrt(c) too large. It must be log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c)*lambda_x^c)) * artanh(sqrt(c)*||w||) * w/||w||. Numerical evidence at c=0.25: log_0^c(exp_0^c(v)) returns 2v instead of v, violating the spec's own conventions.tangent_norm identity log_0^c(exp_0^c(v)) = v; the stated form also has no finite c->0 limit, so switch_geometry's claim that the behaviour field is unchanged in the euclid branch (n_i, m_i keep their values) is impossible.

Gradient path: the idea says gradients flow through v_i and u_k, but loss_total asserts 'NO term in C or q enters the loss' (cost = decision variable) and the mechanism calls the idea's claim 'withdrawn'; simultaneously computations.sinkhorn_plan and computations.nearest_code_distance are marked differentiable: true, computations.arc_length is marked differentiable: true although its own note says 'no gradient path runs through m_i', and loss_total keeps 'plus whatever plan term the baseline already has', which would carry C's gradient into v_i and u_k. One path must be stated: either the cost/plan contributes a differentiable term to the loss (then loss_total must contain it and v_i, u_k do receive gradient, restoring the idea) or it does not (then sinkhorn_plan, nearest_code_distance and arc_length must be differentiable: false and the plan-term clause must be removed).

computations.behaviour_magnitude: M_i = lambda_{v_i}*||t_i|| is used, whereas the idea's raw magnitude is M_i = ||t_i||. lambda_{v_i} = 2/(1-c||v_i||^2) is 2 at the origin and unbounded near the boundary, so both the clip m_i = min(M_i, 0.5*d_nn_i) and the resulting Mobius displacement are inflated by at least a factor 2 relative to the idea. Either set M_i = ||t_i|| as the idea states, or state explicitly that the idea's raw magnitude is replaced by the Riemannian tangent norm and that every arc length and displacement is rescaled by lambda_{v_i} >= 2.

computations.poincare_cost: d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||) is twice the idea's d_P = (1/sqrt(c))*artanh(...). C is fed unchanged to the baseline Sinkhorn with the baseline epsilon, so doubling the cost halves the effective entropic temperature and changes the plan; the 'factor 2 changes no argmin' argument in switch_geometry covers only an argmin, which the mechanism explicitly does not take. Either use the idea's (1/sqrt(c)) prefactor (then the c->0 limit is ||x-y||, not 2||x-y||, and switch_geometry must say so) or keep the factor 2 and state that the cost is the idea's cost doubled and that the baseline epsilon is doubled with it.

STEP 1 — goal: read the specification against the idea and list candidate defects.
Read: (there is no workspace file; the idea, idea equations, idea coupling/ablations and the full specification are in the task text).
Observations (candidate defects):
(1) computations.quantised_value: definition "x_q = P + (one_hot(k_l(i)) - P).detach()" has forward value one_hot(k_l(i)), i.e. shape B x K = B x 256, while the output field claims "x_q (B x d)" with d = 32 and the note claims "the forward value is exactly the chosen RAW codeword E_{k_l(i)}". Both cannot hold: no codebook multiply appears in the algebraic part. The backward is the identity on P only for the one-hot form; a codeword-valued form x_q = P@E + (E_k - P@E).detach() has backward E^T into P. The idea itself asserted the same wrong sentence, but the spec is supposed to be mathematically correct, so this must be repaired.

findings: continuous_surface.executable_statements: `a = a / q_l` overwrites the codebook with the scaled copy and `e_l = p_i @ a` then builds the quantised vector from E_k/q_l, so the decoder would be fed the SCALED codebook, not the raw codeword. quantised_value, reconstruction and training_integration require the forward value to be exactly the raw, unlifted E_{k_l(i)}; the scaled copy must be a separate variable used only for the lift (`b = lift(E/q_l, c)`), and `e_l` must use the raw E.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: the residual recursion is `r_next = r - e_l` while `r` has already been divided by q_l and `e_l` is also in q_l units, and the `.detach()` of the declared value chain is missing. Re-entering the block with `r = r / q_l` divides the level-3 residual by q_2*q_3 instead of q_3. It must be `r_next = (r_l - E_{k_l}).detach()` in RAW units, normalised once by q_3, exactly as the gradient_rules and level_residual state.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: `d_nn_i = dist(u, b, c)` and `demand_i = (tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)/sqrt(c)) * n_i` are built with the SAME c symbol as the cost, so GEOM=euclid (c := 0) also changes the behaviour field: d_nn_i becomes 2||v_i-u_k||, m_i = min(M_i,0.5*d_nn) and Delta_i change, and the arm no longer 'displaces the codes exactly as the curved arm does'. The field must use a separate frozen constant c_field = 1 (lift, log, d_nn, Delta) in both arms, and only the lift/addition/distance of the COST must take the switch's c.

continuous_surface.executable_statements: `def lift` divides by `sqrt(c)*_norm(v) + eps`, a pole guard that returns ~||v||^2/eps for small ||v|| instead of the vector itself. This contradicts ball_lift's explicit tanhc limit (tanhc(0) = 1, 'no 1e-12 guard stands in for the limit'); the zero limit must be an explicit branch or analytic limit, not an additive epsilon in the denominator.

gradient_rules / residual chain: the specification makes the fine levels' item points v_i constants ('It does NOT reach the fine levels' item points v_i', residual = (residual - quant).detach()), whereas the idea states 'gradients flow only through v_i and u_k'. The cost's gradient therefore never reaches the encoder at levels 2 and 3, changing which parameters the fine-level cost trains; either the fine-level residual must be kept differentiable (no detach) so v_i is in the path, or this must be declared as an explicit recorded amendment, like the factor-2 correction, instead of being justified as 'what the baseline's quantizer already does'.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

Mercer kernel is used to map data from input space to reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) by kernel adaptive filter (KAF). The Kernel adaptive filtering algorithm is superior to common adaptive filtering algorithm in solving nonlinear problems and nonlinear channel equalization. papers.abstract: Abstract The proposed algorithm in this paper is the Quantized Minimum Kernel Risk Hyperbolic Secant Adaptive Filtering Algorithm, which offers a simplified approach to enhancing the performance and stability of kernel adaptive filtering in non-Gaussian noise environments. The algorithm features a newly developed Minimum Kernel Risk Hyperbolic Secant Cost Function, which harnesses the hyperbolic secant function’s strengths to diminish outlier impacts and expedite convergence. In addition, its convex kernel risk-sensitive loss surface facilitates swift and accurate filtering via gradient-based methods , thus ensuring outlier robustness. This method could effectively manage network size and reduce computational complexity by incorporating vector quantization for inputting spatial data. Simulation tests in Mackey-Glass time series prediction and nonlinear system identification have indicated that the Minimum Kernel Hyperbolic Secant Adaptive Filtering Algorithm and its quantized variant excel in terms of convergence speed, robustness, and computational efficiency.

papers.abstract: We present a novel vector quantization (VQ) module for the two state-of-the-art long-range simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms. The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. The HGCN vector quantizes the SURF feature space, leading to a bag-of-word (BoW) representation construction of the images. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.abstract: Vector Quantized Variational AutoEncoders (VQ-VAEs) are designed to compress a continuous input to a discrete latent space and reconstruct it with minimal distortion. They operate by maintaining a set of vectors -- often referred to as the codebook -- and quantizing each encoder output to the nearest vector in the codebook. However, as vector quantization is non-differentiable, the gradient to the encoder flows around the vector quantization layer rather than through it in a straight-through approximation. This approximation may be undesirable as all information from the vector quantization operation is lost. In this work, we propose a way to propagate gradients through the vector quantization layer of VQ-VAEs. We smoothly transform each encoder output into its corresponding codebook vector via a rotation and rescaling linear transformation that is treated as a constant during backpropagation. As a result, the relative magnitude and angle between encoder output and codebook vector becomes encoded into the gradient as it propagates through the vector quantization layer and back to the encoder. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. The conclusion of the analysis is that linear-transform coding vector quantizers outperform full-search vector quantizers and warping hyperbolic-tangent neural networks, in terms of performance, complexity and robustness, for a CMOS imaging sensor implemen
papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Abstract The proposed algorithm in this paper is the Quantized Minimum Kernel Risk Hyperbolic Secant Adaptive Filtering Algorithm, which offers a simplified approach to enhancing the performance and stability of kernel adaptive filtering in non-Gaussian noise environments. The algorithm features a newly developed Minimum Kernel Risk Hyperbolic Secant Cost Function, which harnesses the hyperbolic secant function’s strengths to diminish outlier impacts and expedite convergence. In addition, its convex kernel risk-sensitive loss surface facilitates swift and accurate filtering via gradient-based methods , thus ensuring outlier robustness. This method could effectively manage network size and reduce computational complexity by incorporating vector quantization for inputting spatial data. Simulation tests in Mackey-Glass time series prediction and nonlinear system identification have indicated that the Minimum Kernel Hyperbolic Secant Adaptive Filtering Algorithm and its quantized variant excel in terms of convergence speed, robustness, and computational efficiency.

papers.abstract: We present a novel vector quantization (VQ) module for the two state-of-the-art long-range simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms. The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. The HGCN vector quantizes the SURF feature space, leading to a bag-of-word (BoW) representation construction of the images. This representation is subsequently used to determine LCD accuracy and recall. Our approaches in this study are referred to as HGCN-FABMAP and HGCN-ORB. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.abstract: Vector Quantized Variational AutoEncoders (VQ-VAEs) are designed to compress a continuous input to a discrete latent space and reconstruct it with minimal distortion. They operate by maintaining a set of vectors -- often referred to as the codebook -- and quantizing each encoder output to the nearest vector in the codebook. However, as vector quantization is non-differentiable, the gradient to the encoder flows around the vector quantization layer rather than through it in a straight-through approximation. This approximation may be undesirable as all information from the vector quantization operation is lost. In this work, we propose a way to propagate gradients through the vector quantization layer of VQ-VAEs. We smoothly transform each encoder output into its corresponding codebook vector via a rotation and rescaling linear transformation that is treated as a constant during backpropagation. As a result, the relative magnitude and angle between encoder output and codebook vector becomes encoded into the gradient as it propagates through the vector quantization layer and back to the encoder. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.title: HVQ-VAE: Variational auto-encoder with hyperbolic vector quantization

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc
